stem:
Meera wants to find out whether the temperature of the oil affects how much a pakora puffs up when it is fried.

She plans two trials. In Trial 1 she uses oil at 150°C. In Trial 2 she uses oil at 180°C.

For the test to be fair, what should she do about the size of the pakoras and the time they are fried?

options.text: Use pakoras of the same size and fry them for the same time.
Use a bigger pakora in the hotter oil so it puffs up more easily.
Fry the pakora in the hotter oil for a longer time to get a clearer result.
Change both the pakora size and the frying time so the two trials are clearly different.

teacher.key_rationale: In a fair test only the factor being tested (oil temperature) changes; pakora size and frying time must be kept identical, so A is correct. B, C and D each change an extra condition alongside temperature.
